title: FAQs
content:
## Frequently Asked Questions

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="What is Emergent?">
Emergent is an agentic vibe-coding platform where you describe an app in natural language and AI agents build, test, and deploy it for you. You chat with the platform, refine your vision iteratively, and Emergent handles the implementation—front-end, back-end, database, hosting, and deployment.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How does the chat-to-deployment flow work?">
You describe your app idea in the chat interface. Emergent's AI agents interpret your requirements, generate code, provision infrastructure, and deploy a working application. You can refine and iterate by continuing the conversation. For a detailed walkthrough, see [The chat-to-deployment flow](/the-chat-to-deployment-flow).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Do I need to know how to code?">
No. Emergent is designed for users of all technical levels. You describe what you want in plain language, and the platform handles the technical implementation. If you *do* know how to code, you can also provide detailed technical guidance or even paste code snippets to steer the agents.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What types of applications can I build?">
Emergent supports a wide range of applications including web apps, mobile apps (iOS and Android via React Native), dashboards, APIs, SaaS tools, MVPs, prototypes, and internal business tools. The platform handles full-stack development with database integration, authentication, payments, and more.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I convert a web app to mobile or vice versa?">
Yes. Emergent can convert web applications to React Native mobile apps and vice versa. The conversion process preserves your data and core functionality while adapting the UI and navigation patterns for the target platform. See [Web ↔ Mobile conversion](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical) for details.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What technologies does Emergent use under the hood?">
Emergent builds apps using modern, production-ready stacks:

- **Front-end:** React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui components
- **Mobile:** React Native with Expo
- **Back-end:** Node.js, serverless functions, REST and GraphQL APIs
- **Database:** MongoDB Atlas (managed, scalable)
- **Hosting:** Vercel for web, Expo Application Services for mobile
- **Authentication:** Clerk, Auth0, or custom implementations
- **Payments:** Stripe integration

The specific stack may vary based on your app's requirements.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How is my data stored and secured?">
Data is stored in a dedicated MongoDB Atlas database provisioned for your project. Each app gets its own isolated database with industry-standard encryption at rest and in transit. You own your data and can export it at any time. See [Database (MongoDB)](/database-mongodb) for more.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I use my own API keys or bring my own LLM?">
Yes. Emergent provides a [Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) for convenience, but you can bring your own API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or other providers. You can configure per-project LLM preferences and manage keys in your workspace settings.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I deploy my app to production?">
Deployment happens automatically as part of the chat-to-deployment flow. Emergent provisions hosting (Vercel for web, Expo for mobile), configures environment variables, and pushes your app live. You get a live URL immediately. You can also connect a [custom domain](/custom-domain) to your deployed app.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I connect a custom domain to my app?">
Yes. Once your app is deployed, you can connect your own domain name through the workspace settings. Emergent handles DNS configuration and SSL certificate provisioning. See [Custom domain](/custom-domain) for step-by-step instructions.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What happens if I want to iterate or make changes after deployment?">
Continue the conversation in chat. Describe the changes you want, and Emergent's agents will update the code, re-run tests, and deploy the new version. Your database and user data persist across iterations.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I export my code and self-host?">
Yes. You have full access to your application's source code through the workspace. You can export the codebase, clone the repository, and deploy it to any hosting provider you choose. Emergent does not lock you in.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Does Emergent support authentication and user management?">
Yes. You can request user authentication as part of your app requirements. Emergent integrates providers like Clerk, Auth0, or custom auth implementations with email/password, social logins, magic links, and role-based access control.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I integrate third-party APIs and services?">
Absolutely. Tell Emergent which APIs or services you want to integrate (Stripe, Twilio, SendGrid, Google Maps, etc.), and the agents will generate the integration code, handle authentication, and configure environment variables.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I manage environment variables and secrets?">
Environment variables and secrets are managed through the workspace settings. You can add, edit, or remove variables, and they are securely injected into your app at build and runtime. Secrets are encrypted and never exposed in the codebase.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What is the workspace and how do I navigate it?">
The workspace is your project hub where you can view code, logs, database records, deployment history, settings, and more. It provides a visual interface for monitoring and managing your app. See [A tour of the workspace](/a-tour-of-the-workspace) for a complete overview.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I collaborate with a team on an Emergent project?">
Team collaboration features vary by plan. You can invite collaborators to view or edit projects, manage permissions, and work together in the same workspace. Check your plan details for collaboration limits.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What are the pricing plans and limits?">
Emergent offers multiple pricing tiers with different quotas for projects, deployments, compute, storage, and team members. Visit the Emergent pricing page or your account dashboard for the latest plan details and limits.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I upgrade or downgrade my plan?">
You can change your subscription tier at any time from the billing section of your account settings. Upgrades take effect immediately; downgrades apply at the end of the current billing cycle.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What happens if I hit a usage limit?">
If you reach a plan limit (projects, API calls, storage, etc.), you'll receive a notification. Depending on the limit, the platform may pause certain operations until you upgrade or the next billing cycle begins. Critical functionality like accessing your code and data remains available.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I cancel my subscription at any time?">
Yes. You can cancel your subscription from the billing settings. Your access continues until the end of the current billing period, after which your account transitions to a free or read-only tier (depending on plan structure).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What support options are available?">
Support options depend on your plan. All users have access to documentation, community forums, and email support. Higher-tier plans may include priority support, dedicated Slack channels, or live onboarding sessions.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I report a bug or request a feature?">
Use the feedback widget in the workspace, or contact support via email. Feature requests are tracked and prioritized based on user demand. You can also join the Emergent community to vote on and discuss upcoming features.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Is there a limit to how many times I can iterate on an app?">
Iteration limits depend on your plan. Most plans allow unlimited iterations within reasonable usage bounds. Compute-intensive operations (like full re-builds) may count toward usage quotas.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I build apps in languages other than English?">
Yes. Emergent supports natural-language input in multiple languages. You can describe your app in your preferred language, and the platform will generate code and content accordingly.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Does Emergent support internationalization (i18n) in apps?">
Yes. You can request multi-language support for your app, and Emergent will generate i18n-ready code with locale management, translation keys, and language switchers.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What testing does Emergent perform on my app?">
Emergent's agents run automated tests during the build process, including unit tests, integration tests, and basic end-to-end smoke tests. You can also request additional test coverage or specific testing scenarios.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I access the database directly?">
Yes. You can query and manage your MongoDB database through the workspace interface or by connecting directly using MongoDB clients with the provided connection string.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I back up my database?">
MongoDB Atlas (Emergent's database provider) performs automatic backups. You can also export your data manually from the workspace or configure additional backup policies through Atlas settings.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What happens to my data if I delete a project?">
<Warning>
Deleting a project permanently removes the codebase, database, and all associated resources. This action cannot be undone. Always export your code and data before deletion.
</Warning>
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I import an existing codebase into Emergent?">
Currently, Emergent is optimized for greenfield projects (building from scratch). Importing existing codebases is not directly supported, but you can describe your existing app and Emergent can recreate or extend it.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Does Emergent support mobile app store deployment?">
Yes. For React Native apps, Emergent integrates with Expo Application Services (EAS) to build and submit apps to the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. You'll need developer accounts with Apple and Google.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How do I handle app updates after publishing to app stores?">
Continue iterating in Emergent as usual. When you're ready to release an update, Emergent can rebuild and submit the new version through EAS. You control the release schedule and versioning.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What are the system requirements for using Emergent?">
Emergent is a cloud-based platform accessible via any modern web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge). No local installation or specific hardware is required. For mobile app testing, you can use simulators (included) or physical devices.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I use Emergent offline?">
No. Emergent is a cloud platform that requires an internet connection for the AI agents to build, test, and deploy your apps.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Where can I learn more about Emergent-specific terminology?">
See the [Glossary of Emergent terms](/glossary-of-emergent-terms) for definitions of platform-specific concepts like agents, vibes, canonical builds, and more.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="How does Emergent handle versioning and rollbacks?">
Emergent maintains a deployment history in the workspace. You can view past versions and roll back to a previous deployment if needed. Each deployment is tagged with a timestamp and changelog.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I schedule deployments or automate workflows?">
Advanced automation features (like scheduled deployments or CI/CD integrations) may be available on higher-tier plans or through API access. Check your plan details or contact support for specifics.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What happens if an agent makes a mistake or breaks my app?">
Emergent agents are designed to test and validate changes before deployment. If an issue occurs, you can roll back to a previous version, describe the problem in chat, and the agents will attempt to fix it. You can also manually edit code in the workspace.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Is my intellectual property protected?">
Yes. You retain full ownership of the applications and content you create with Emergent. Emergent does not claim ownership of your ideas, code, or data.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Does Emergent comply with data protection regulations (GDPR, etc.)?">
Emergent follows industry best practices for data security and privacy. For specific compliance questions or data processing agreements, contact the Emergent legal or support team.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I white-label or resell apps built on Emergent?">
Yes. You own the apps you build and can white-label, resell, or commercialize them as you see fit. Check your plan's terms of service for any restrictions.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

<Callout type="info" title="Still have questions?">
If your question isn't answered here, check the rest of the documentation or reach out to Emergent support. We're here to help you succeed.
</Callout>
